title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sits within Grothendieck's 1965 notes on the Galois theory of motives. It sets out the realization fibre functors attached to points of a base X, presumably as part of a Tannakian formalism for motives over X with coefficients. The surrounding pages are unrelated Bourbaki typescripts reused as scrap paper.

The first line ends a previous item. Something is taken "par Q_ell(k)", which is "particularly interesting when k is a number field". This most likely refers to ell-adic realizations with Galois action, giving representations of Gal(kbar/k) when k is arithmetic.

Item (iv): to a point x with values in C corresponds an integral fibre functor xi_{x,Z}, an object of T_?(Z). This is presumably the category or torsor of fibre functors with values in finitely generated Z-modules. Its value on a motive F is the realization of F in the fibre F_x, in modern terms the Betti realization H_B(F_x, Z). It comes with canonical comparison isomorphisms:
- xi_{x,Z} ⊗_Z Z_ell ≅ xi_{x,ell}, the ell-adic fibre functor (the Artin comparison between singular and étale cohomology);
- xi_{x,Z} ⊗_Z C ≅ xi_{x,infinity}, the complex (de Rham or analytic) fibre functor.

Grothendieck then observes that xi_{x,Z} really depends only on a point with values in a topological field K isomorphic to C, without choosing the isomorphism. Hence complex conjugation gives a canonical involutive isomorphism xi_{x,Z} ≅ xi_{tau x,Z}, where tau x is the conjugate point. Modern name: the F_infinity / real-structure action on Betti cohomology induced by the antiholomorphic homeomorphism X_sigma(C) → X_{sigma-bar}(C).

Finally he plans a refinement for a scheme point x of X:
(a) if k(x) is dense in C, xi_{x,Z} depends only on an archimedean topology (absolute value) on k(x) with completion C, i.e. on an archimedean place, not an embedding;
(b) the case where k(x) is not dense in C (a real place) is started and cut off at the page end.

The purpose is to make the Betti fibre functors intrinsic: indexed by archimedean places, with the conjugation involution as built-in descent data. This parallels the ell-adic functors being indexed by geometric points.
errors: Taken literally, case (a) is slightly inaccurate. The embedding k(x) → C is determined by the topology only up to complex conjugation. So xi_{x,Z} depends on the place only up to the involutive isomorphism just described, and the functor is canonical only together with that descent datum. Grothendieck's preceding remark supplies exactly this, so it is a matter of phrasing rather than a mistake.
Case b) is unfinished on this page.

ideas.what: Integral Betti fibre functor at a complex point, with comparison isomorphisms to the ell-adic and complex realizations
ideas.modern_name: Betti realization with Artin comparison and Betti–de Rham/analytic comparison; integral structure on realizations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motives programme), formalized by Deligne (Valeurs de fonctions L, 1979) and Jannsen (mixed motives, 1990)
ideas.where_published: Ideas sketched in Grothendieck's letters to Serre (1964–65) and in Saavedra Rivano's thesis; not in this form in EGA/SGA

ideas.what: The Betti fibre functor depends only on a point in a topological field isomorphic to C, giving a canonical involutive isomorphism with the conjugate point's functor
ideas.modern_name: F_infinity (complex-conjugation involution) on Betti cohomology; real Betti structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales, 1979)

ideas.what: Indexing the archimedean fibre functors by archimedean places/topologies on k(x) rather than by embeddings, with a separate real case
ideas.modern_name: Betti realizations attached to archimedean places, the analogue of ell-adic fibre functors at geometric points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne 1979 and in Deligne–Milne / Deligne's Tannakian work

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an early (1965) and clear formulation of the integral Betti fibre functor, its comparisons, and the complex-conjugation descent datum indexed by archimedean places. All of this became standard later (Deligne 1979 and others) and is largely implicit in Grothendieck's known programme. It is of historical interest for dating, but contains nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The first line most likely reads 'par Q_ℓ(k)'; the handwriting is ambiguous but consistent with Q_ℓ.
'(i.e. isom. à C [?])' plausibly reads '(i.e. isom. à C topologiquement)' or similar.
'Il faut définir aussi ... si x est localisation' is more likely 'Il faut dire aussi, si x est un point de X'; 'localisation' is a doubtful reading of the interlinear word.
'ξ_{x,Z} dépend de ξ [?] donnée' should read 'ξ_{x,Z} dépend de la donnée d'une topologie archimédienne (ou valuation) sur k(x), à complété C'.
